breakfast.name: Çörek (Turkmen Bread)
instructions: Make dough, rise 1 hour
Shape into flat rounds
Bake in tandoor or oven at 230°C
breakfast.description: Round bread baked in a clay oven.

breakfast.name: Gatyk (Yogurt)
instructions: Serve thick yogurt with sugar or honey

breakfast.name: Chorek (Turkmen Round Bread)
instructions: Chorek is the Turkmen round flatbread -- baked in a tandoor (tamdyr)
Similar to Uzbek non and Tajik non but with Turkmen character
Baked by sticking to the hot inner wall of the clay oven
The outside: slightly charred, smoky from the tandoor
A sacred food: bread should not be wasted in Turkmen culture
Breaking bread together is a hospitality ritual
breakfast.description: Turkmen round tandoor flatbread -- chorek, leavened dough baked by sticking to the hot inner clay wall of the tamdyr (tandoor). Slightly charred, smoky. Bread is sacred in Turkmen culture; wasting it is disrespectful. Breaking chorek together is the hospitality ritual.

breakfast.name: Salam (Milk and Bread)
instructions: Salam is the simple Turkmen breakfast of bread torn into warm milk
Day-old bread softened in warm milk
Eaten savory (salted) or sweet (sugared)
A poverty-era staple that has become a nostalgic comfort food
Simple, warming, and deeply Turkmen in its frugality -- bread must be used
breakfast.description: Turkmen simple bread in warm milk -- day-old chorek torn into warm milk. Eaten salted or sweetened. A frugal staple from necessity that became a nostalgic comfort food. The Turkmen imperative to never waste bread: even old bread is eaten.

lunch.name: Turkmen Plov (Pilaf)
instructions: Fry onion and lamb
Add carrots and cumin
Add rice and water
Cook covered, add garlic head on top
lunch.description: Central Asian lamb pilaf — Turkmen style.

lunch.name: Çorba (Lamb Soup)
instructions: Simmer lamb 30 min
Add vegetables
Cook 15 more min

lunch.name: Shurpa (Lamb Soup)
instructions: Shurpa is the Central Asian lamb and vegetable soup -- the most common lunch in Turkmenistan
A simple, hearty broth with whole vegetables and bone-in lamb
The lamb is cooked for a long time -- the marrow enriches the broth
The vegetables are added whole or in large pieces -- they cook in the lamb broth
Served with fresh bread
Eaten at home and at teahouses (chai khane)
lunch.description: Turkmen lamb and vegetable soup -- bone-in lamb simmered for a long time (marrow enriching the broth) with whole potatoes, carrots, and turnips. The most common Turkmen lunch. Eaten with fresh bread at home and at chai khane (teahouses).

lunch.name: Gutap (Stuffed Flatbread)
ingredients: Filling: pumpkin and onion OR greens and spring onion
instructions: Gutap are the Turkmen stuffed flatbreads -- similar to Tajik sambusa but pan-cooked
A thin unleavened dough
Stuffed with pumpkin and onion (the most popular) or fresh greens
Folded into a half-moon shape and cooked on a griddle
Eaten as a snack, bread substitute, or main
The pumpkin filling sweetens slightly as it cooks
lunch.description: Turkmen stuffed flatbread -- gutap, unleavened dough folded around a pumpkin-onion filling (or fresh greens), cooked on a griddle. The pumpkin filling sweetens as it cooks. A snack, bread substitute, or light main.

lunch.name: Dovga (Yoghurt Soup)
ingredients: Rice (cooked or added raw to cook in the soup)
Fresh herbs: dill, coriander, spring onion
instructions: Dovga is the Turkmen yoghurt soup -- similar to Azerbaijani and Persian yoghurt soups
Yoghurt stabilized with egg (so it does not curdle when heated)
Rice and herbs cooked in the yoghurt
The result: a thick, tangy, herby soup
Served warm or cold
The herb quantity: very generous -- it should be green
A cooling summer soup
lunch.description: Turkmen yoghurt soup -- dovga, yoghurt stabilized with egg and heated with rice and generous fresh herbs (dill, coriander, spring onion). The soup stays tangy and silky from the egg stabilization. Served warm or cold. Related to Azerbaijani and Persian yoghurt soups.

dinner.name: Manti (Steamed Dumplings)
instructions: Make dough, roll wrappers
Mix filling
Fill, pinch closed
Steam 30 min
Serve with garlic yogurt

dinner.name: Shashlik (Grilled Kebab)
instructions: Marinate lamb in onion and vinegar
Thread on skewers
Grill over charcoal

dinner.name: Kabap (Charcoal Grilled Lamb)
instructions: Kabap is the Central Asian grilled meat -- universal across Turkmenistan
Ground lamb pressed onto wide metal skewers (kofte style) or lamb chunks
Seasoned simply: cumin, onion, salt
Grilled over charcoal -- the fat drips and creates the char
Served with flatbread, raw onion, and tomato
dinner.description: Turkmen charcoal lamb skewers -- ground lamb pressed onto metal skewers with onion and cumin, grilled over charcoal. The dripping fat and charcoal create the flavor. Served with flatbread, raw onion, and tomato.

dinner.name: Yarma (Cracked Wheat Porridge)
instructions: Yarma is the Turkmen cracked wheat porridge -- a savory, hearty dinner
Cracked wheat cooked in lamb broth until soft and thick
Finished with butter
A simple, nourishing grain dish
The nomadic food tradition: grains and lamb are the diet foundation
dinner.description: Turkmen cracked wheat porridge -- yarma, coarse cracked wheat cooked in lamb broth until thick, finished with butter. Simple and nourishing. The nomadic diet foundation of grain and lamb.

dinner.name: Manty (Steamed Dumplings)
instructions: Manty are the Central Asian large steamed dumplings
The Turkmen version: large, filled with lamb and onion
Steamed in a tiered pot
Served with sour cream or yoghurt
Part of the Silk Road dumpling family (Turkish manti, Mongolian buuz, Uzbek manti)
The Turkmen name is borrowed from the Turkish/Chinese via the Silk Road
dinner.description: Turkmen large steamed dumplings -- manty, thin dough filled with ground lamb and onion, steamed in a tiered pot. Served with sour cream or yoghurt. Part of the Silk Road dumpling family: Turkish manti, Mongolian buuz, the name traveling the trade route.

snacks.name: Somsa (Baked Pastry)
instructions: Fill dough with lamb
Shape triangles
Top with sesame
Bake at 200°C 25 min

snacks.name: Watermelon (Karpyz)
ingredients: Karpyz (Turkmen watermelon -- some of the finest in the world)
instructions: Turkmenistan grows some of the finest watermelons in the world
The Turkmen desert climate: hot days, cool nights -- ideal for developing sugar
Karpyz (watermelon) is a national pride
The Ashgabat watermelon market is famous
A September watermelon festival celebrates the harvest
Eaten after meals as a dessert or throughout the day as a snack
snacks.description: Turkmen prized watermelon -- Turkmenistan grows some of the finest watermelons in the world. The desert climate (hot days, cool nights) concentrates sugar. Karpyz is a national pride with a September harvest festival in Ashgabat. Eaten as a dessert or throughout the day.

snacks.name: Qurt (Dried Yoghurt)
instructions: Qurt are the Turkmen dried yoghurt balls (same as Tajik qurut)
Strained yoghurt, salted, formed into balls, and sun-dried
Intensely sour and salty
A shelf-stable protein snack from the nomadic herder tradition
Eaten as a snack on its own or dissolved in water for a sauce
snacks.description: Turkmen dried yoghurt balls -- qurt, strained yoghurt salted and sun-dried into shelf-stable balls. Intensely sour and salty. The nomadic herder preservation technique. Eaten as a snack or dissolved for sauce.

snacks.name: Semeni (Sprouted Wheat Sweet)
instructions: Semeni is the Turkmen Nowruz sweet -- made from sprouted wheat
Wheat berries are soaked and sprouted until the sprouts are about 1cm
Ground and cooked slowly until they develop into a thick, sweet, caramel-like paste
The natural sugars in the wheat sprout give the sweetness -- no added sugar
Made specifically for Nowruz (Persian New Year, March 21)
The Turkmen Nowruz tradition: semeni symbolizes spring and new life
The sprouting process takes 7-10 days -- planning ahead is required
snacks.description: Turkmen sprouted wheat Nowruz sweet -- wheat sprouted for 7-10 days, ground and slowly cooked until the natural sugars develop into a thick, caramel-like paste (no added sugar). Made specifically for Nowruz (Persian New Year, March 21). The sprouts symbolize spring and new life.

desserts.name: Halva
instructions: Toast flour in butter
Make sugar syrup
Combine, stir until thick

desserts.name: Pishme (Fried Dough Sticks)
instructions: Pishme are the Turkmen fried dough sweets
A rich egg-and-butter dough fried until golden
Dusted with icing sugar
Eaten at celebrations and Nowruz
Similar to other Central Asian fried dough sweets
desserts.description: Turkmen fried dough sweets -- pishme, rich egg-and-butter dough fried golden and dusted with icing sugar. Eaten at celebrations and Nowruz.

desserts.name: Halwa (Flour Sweet)
instructions: Turkmen halwa is the flour halva -- toasted flour in butter
Flour fried in butter until golden and nutty
Sugar and water added to form a thick paste
Eaten at funerals, weddings, and Nowruz
The same dish exists across Central Asia
desserts.description: Turkmen flour halva -- flour toasted in butter until golden and nutty, water and sugar added into a thick paste. Eaten at funerals, weddings, and Nowruz. The Central Asian flour sweet.

drinks.name: Çal (Fermented Camel Milk)
instructions: Add starter to camel milk
Ferment 1-2 days
Serve cold
drinks.description: Fermented camel milk — prized in the Karakum Desert.

drinks.name: Green Tea
instructions: Brew green tea in a pot
Serve hot
drinks.description: Green tea — Turkmenistan's national beverage, drunk all day.

drinks.name: Green Tea (Gok Chay)
ingredients: Green tea (Chinese-origin, brought via Silk Road)
instructions: Gok chay (green tea) is the drink of Turkmenistan
The Silk Road: Chinese green tea traveled through Central Asia
Brewed in a teapot -- never with boiling water (it turns bitter)
Drunk at all times and offered to every guest
The chai khane (teahouse) is the Turkmen social center
Green tea is preferred in Turkmenistan; black tea in other Central Asian countries
drinks.description: Turkmen green tea -- gok chay, Chinese green tea via the Silk Road, brewed in a teapot with hot (not boiling) water. Offered to every guest. The chai khane (teahouse) is the social center. Turkmenistan prefers green tea; most neighboring countries drink black tea.
